subject: Private VPC discovery recap — FinHealth (regulated workloads, KMS, air-gap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finhealth.com>, Tom Hernandez <tom.hernandez@finhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC discovery recap — FinHealth (regulated workloads, KMS, air-gap)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Nice to meet you both. Below is a quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points
- PHI and PII handling across inference flows (customer messaging + clinical notes) — must meet internal legal controls and external auditors.
- Current inference latency and cost at peak hours is causing throttling of features for clinical staff.
- Security team requires strict egress controls and customer-managed key usage for model artifacts and logs.

Current stack / constraints
- On-prem primary data store + AWS-only compute for analytics.
- Network: customers run across isolated VPCs; no direct internet access from some processing subnets (air-gapped workflows for batch jobs).
- Key management: FinHealth uses AWS KMS with a requirement to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM-backed CMKs.
- Compliance: preparing for an upcoming audit; SOC 2 + HITRUST posture matters.

Success criteria (what FinHealth will measure)
1) Private deployment that ensures no PHI leaves customer-managed network boundaries unless explicitly allowed.
2) Integration with customer KMS for encryption-at-rest of model artifacts and audit-proof key usage.
3) Latency SLOs for synchronous features: p95 < 400ms for short inference paths (subject to model selection).
4) Clear runbook for emergency rollback and fail-open behaviors during service degradation.

Technical requirements we discussed
- Private control plane or isolated connectivity to Redwood Private (VPN or VPC peering) — FinHealth prefers VPC peering with strict route tables.
- Option for fully disconnected on-prem package for air-gap batch inference pipelines.
- Support for BYOK/HSM integration (AWS KMS CMK + importable keys) and audit logs exported to FinHealth SIEM.
- Ability to pin model versions and run canary rollouts inside FinHealth environment.

Next steps
1) I’ll loop in Dylan (solutions engineering) and Connor (security) to scope a short tech workshop to validate the network and KMS approach (provisionally 60–90 minutes).
2) FinHealth to share redacted VPC network diagram and any security questionnaire (I attached a sample we typically get filled out).
3) Redwood to prepare a checklist for on-prem/offline deployment and an initial cost estimate for a Dedicated/VPC deployment.

Attachments: FinHealth_Security_Questionnaire_Sample.pdf, VPC_Network_Diagram.png

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Private VPC discovery recap — FinHealth (regulated workloads, KMS, air-gap)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed recap — that captures our requirements well. A few clarifications from our side:

- VPC peering: preferred. We cannot allow outbound internet from the inference subnets unless tightly controlled.
- KMS: must be HSM-backed CMKs; security will validate that Redwood does not retain any plaintext key material.
- Air-gap: For certain monthly batch processes we need an on-prem appliance or fully offline package.
- Auditing: all model access and key usage logs must be available for export to our Splunk instance.

We can share a redacted VPC diagram and a completed version of the questionnaire by EOD Wednesday. Can Dylan/Connor and Marissa propose 60-minute meeting times for next week?

Best,
Sara
Director of IT Security, FinHealth

- Confirm support for BYOK/HSM (we need to detail the flow: CMK in FinHealth account, Redwood never sees private key material; keys used to wrap model artifacts/records).
